subject.title: [Feature]: Per-agent cost budget enforcement at the gateway level

question: Should per-agent spend limits be a native core gateway feature, a new blocking plugin/API seam, or deferred to external/provider budget controls?
rationale: The fix adds config/defaults, provider dispatch admission policy, durable accounting semantics, and operator UX; automation cannot safely choose the product boundary or upgrade contract.

options.title: Design native gateway budgets
options.body: Define a default-unlimited core budget contract with reservations, receipts, status/doctor output, and upgrade-safe config before implementation.

options.title: Expose blocking plugin/API admission
options.body: Keep budget policy outside core but add the missing synchronous pre-model-call estimate/reservation hook needed for reliable external enforcement.

options.title: Defer to external/provider controls
options.body: Document provider dashboards, proxies, and per-account approaches as the supported path and close or narrow this issue to missing extension APIs only.

recommendation.title: Design native gateway budgets
recommendation.body: Define a default-unlimited core budget contract with reservations, receipts, status/doctor output, and upgrade-safe config before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent history on cost/usage visibility and related product-scoping discussions for outbound governance.
